pull_request.body:
## Problem

Fresh sessions are still instructed to finish Draft PR #149 even though #149, #154, #150, #155 and #156 are merged. Repeated active-state snapshots in START_HERE and stale status assertions preserve the wrong stopping point.

## Changes

Correct current-state, roadmap, risk and continuation references; reduce START_HERE to navigation and invariant reminders; index exact physical records from #149/#154/#150 with direct source links. Identify open #151 as research-only, without adopting its architecture or authorizing a new provider. Align two existing documentation assertions with the recorded bounded acceptance.

Historical evidence remains precise: #149 used an owner waiver for that merge only; #154 has its own fresh review and physical suite. #150 physical evidence proves install/blocked-target/tray-restart continuity, not a successful accepted-main transition. Its final fresh-review result was not found in the inspected PR timeline; merged metadata is not a PASS substitute.

## Validation and scope

55 existing documentation/architecture/research/acceptance-contract tests passed; git diff --check passed. API-published tree matches the locally validated tree exactly.

Failure-class closure: stale duplicated active-state prose -> multiple status owners -> search of current operating docs and adjacent consumers -> remove START_HERE's duplicate snapshot and retain CURRENT_STATE as the current-work owner. Existing documentation checks remain in use.

Repository skill bootstrap performed at main 5dc3d2f44dd74b99f781311c75f8c4023c5f2a7c. This is a documentation/status correction and two documentation-only assertion updates; it changes no runtime, authority, physical acceptance criteria, or merge/review policy. No new Stage Research or physical qualification is required for this correction. The existing independent-review exception for non-material documentation applies. Hosted checks still must pass before merge.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the immediate work aligned with the roadmap**

The roadmap still defines automatic-reviewer migration as the next release-critical item (`ROADMAP.md` lines 57–62), but this new immediate-critical-path section directs fresh sessions to PR #151's execution-adapter/persistent-session research and onward implementation instead. Following `CURRENT_STATE.md` will therefore skip or reorder the reviewer migration—the same continuation failure this change is intended to prevent. Either place #151 explicitly ahead of the migration in the roadmap or keep it out of the immediate path.
